Use case: precise-object-edit. Image 1 is the EDIT TARGET: the existing wide retro Maryland arena hero image. Image 2 is a REFERENCE ONLY: a basketball court marking/dimension diagram supplied by the user. Edit image 1; do not output the diagram.

Arena cleanup:
1. At the TOP TIER of bleachers, remove the malformed dark entry/tunnel openings that blend into the seats and stairways. Replace these openings with continuous, evenly spaced concrete STAIR STEPS that extend each existing aisle all the way up through that top seating tier. Maintain clean straight separations between stair aisles and the black seat blocks; no doors/tunnels at the tops of those aisles.
2. In the MIDDLE HORIZONTAL CONCOURSE LEVEL of warm yellow-lit entrances / open box bays, remove ALL the blurry, ghostlike, half-formed black chair silhouettes sitting inside those bays. Make the bays clean empty architectural entrance spaces with consistent floor, walls, and railings. Keep their warm lighting, structural columns, and real entrance doors. Do NOT remove the clearly defined black bleacher seating, gold courtside seats, or black foreground seat backs.
3. Keep the two previously cleared courtside stair entrances open. Keep both repaired black/yellow shot clocks legibly reading '24', and the central HOME 00 / GUEST 00 scoreboard.

Court correction, using IMAGE 2 AS THE AUTHORITATIVE GEOMETRY REFERENCE:
Remove the inaccurate existing floor linework and redraw the complete court as a single coherent, symmetric, properly proportioned marking layout projected onto the existing floor plane. The playing rectangle is 94 ft long (left to right in this view) by 50 ft wide (far to near sideline). Use one consistent perspective / vanishing geometry for every floor marking. White perimeter boundary, center line perpendicular to sidelines, 6-ft-radius center circle at exact midpoint. Both rectangular painted lanes must be 16 ft wide and 19 ft deep from baseline to free throw line. Rims centered on the lanes, 5 ft 3 in inside each baseline; backboards 4 ft inside baselines. Free throw circles 6 ft radius, with the half-circle inside each painted lane dashed and the half outside solid. Restricted area semicircles 4 ft radius centered below each rim. Three-point arcs 23 ft 9 in radius from the basket centers, smoothly joining the straight corner-three segments which are 3 ft inside each sideline (22 ft from the basket across the width). Add tidy lane-space hash marks and short sideline ticks matching the reference. Both halves must mirror exactly in court coordinates. Circles become correct perspective ellipses on this floor. No extra cross-court horizontal lines, no doubled/overlapping court layouts, no stray white fragments, no wobbly arcs. Make all paint strokes crisp with consistent width. Preserve golden hardwood, black painted lane interiors, black/gold court border, and the red Maryland M and Maryland flag emblem at center court; integrate the correct visible white center circle and centerline cleanly with the emblem. The floor should read as the exact court in reference 2 with Maryland branding, seen from the same arena camera as image 1, not as a flat diagram pasted into the image. Do not print measurement numbers, arrows, dimensions, or diagram annotations on the floor.

General: clean up obvious smudged or impossible small architectural details and broken floor reflections, but keep the camera viewpoint, wide aspect ratio, framing, Maryland flag ribbon displays, arena lighting, basket positions, polished wood reflections, and the recognizable retro 3D/pixel video game rendering style. No people, portraits, UI, website text, new decorations, or watermark. Output just the complete improved arena image.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Image 1 is the edited Maryland arena target. Image 2 is the authoritative court geometry reference. The architecture is now correct: preserve the clean continuous upper stairways, empty yellow-lit midlevel bays, clear lower stair exits, clean seats, scoreboard and 24-second shot clocks EXACTLY.

Refine ONLY THE FLOOR MARKINGS and center emblem scale. The center circle in image 1 is too large relative to the 94-foot court, and some old stray horizontal lines still cut through the painted lanes. Make these precise corrections:
- The center circle must be 12 feet in DIAMETER (6-foot radius), only 12/94 = 12.77 percent of the full court length when measured in the same floor coordinates. At the center depth in this particular frame, its width should be approximately 230 pixels rather than the current approximately 340 pixels. Its height is appropriately foreshortened in the same floor perspective. Render a COMPLETE CLEAN VISIBLE WHITE ELLIPSE, including its front and back edges. Scale the Maryland M/flag center logo down to fit neatly INSIDE that circle, so it no longer hides or overruns the circle. Keep the logo's accurate recognizable shape/colors.
- Use the supplied diagram's EXACT mirrored floor layout. Keep each lane 16 ft wide, 19 ft long, with a single white rectangle perimeter. Remove the extra unrelated white HORIZONTAL STRIPE that currently runs through the inside of each black painted lane near the near-side lane edge. No stray lines inside the paint besides the restricted semicircle and dashed half of the free-throw circle. No second floor layout, ghost line, misplaced cross-court stripe or duplicated border.
- Free throw circles 12 feet diameter, same physical diameter as the center circle. Solid half outside the paint, dashed half inside the paint. Restricted semicircles 8 feet diameter. Maintain 23 feet 9 inches three-point arcs and 3-feet-inset straight corner lines, center line, white boundary, correct short hash marks.
- Both rim centers must be centered across each 16-foot lane, with every circular arc and paint edge sharing a single consistent floor perspective. Match the relative lengths and all marking placements in reference image 2; do not retain source errors just because they are already drawn.

No change to arena geometry, camera, lighting, wood material, overall framing, aspect ratio, seats, or any other object. This is a clean retro video game arena image, not a dimension diagram: no numbers, measurement labels, arrows or UI on the floor.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit this arena image with ONE tiny correction only. There are TWO erroneous thin, perfectly horizontal white stripes INSIDE the BLACK PAINTED LANES. In this 1671 by 942 image, the left erroneous stripe runs approximately from x=0,y=625 to x=366,y=625, and the right erroneous stripe runs from x=1307,y=625 to x=1670,y=625. These stripes are only about 18 pixels above the proper near-side white perimeter edge of each black painted lane, which is at y=643. ERASE those TWO interior white stripes by restoring the clean uninterrupted black glossy paint underneath. KEEP the correct lane perimeter white edges at y=643. Keep the legitimate restricted-area curved semicircles higher up inside the paint, dashed free-throw semicircles, slanted free-throw lines, and short hash marks outside the paint. The unwanted stripes run UNDER the restricted arcs and do not belong on any basketball court. Do not add any other lines or objects. Change no other pixels or features: keep the center-circle and logo, bleachers, stairs, clean midlevel bays, scoreboards, hoops, court lines outside these two thin stray stripes, framing, color, and retro rendering exactly as in the input.
